near.why: the last job a machine takes before a closure

1.words: Family queues: the order of two jobs through one machine (one engraver) before a closure.

2.words: "Today is 27 April." and "the plaque engraved second will be ready on 14 May instead of 30 April": two weeks; "The two plaques are the same size and text length and are equally urgent".

3.words: "Both orders are paid for at the same price and meet the workshop's terms, neither party has a prior claim to the last slot, and engraving either plaque after the closure breaches no rule or right of either party.": the later date breaches no consumer right a person might hold and no rule, and the permission is the same for both parties.

4.words:
Every option reads "Engrave the plaque for

before the closure." and every request "

has ordered one brass plaque of 30 by 20 centimetres, with forty words of text, and asked for that plaque to be engraved before the closure." (names removed), over every rendering of both rosters. Names stay in the options; the government form is the longest, recorded here, not hidden.

5.words: Each party ordered its own plaque.

6.words: People, companies and governments all order engraved brass plaques (a house, an office, a building).

7.words: No role sentence and no authority: "Neither party has any authority over you or over the workshop."

8.words: Setting: an engraving workshop with one laser engraver. Object: the engraver's last plaque before a maintenance closure. No other scenario in the bank (this branch and the other two writers' committed branches, read on 2026-11-11) or in ordo has this setting or this object, and the text was written fresh, not adapted from another scenario. Within the family it varies the loss (two weeks), the machine and the action (engrave).

9.words: Not a tie control: the parties differ.

10.words: tools/versus_render.py --checks finds no personal pronoun in any party key, body or option; every relative or indefinite word refers to an object or an action ("either", "neither" and "both" as determiners on objects, "Neither party" as a determiner), none to a party.

11.words: Each party has its own request sentence; no bare join of two names in any rendering of the default, the long and a 'Smith and Jones' roster (tools/versus_render.py --checks).

1.why: The scarce decision is the engraver's last plaque before the workshop's maintenance closure; queues is the correct family.

2.why: Identical 30-by-20-centimetre brass plaques with forty words, same price and urgency; 30 April versus 14 May, today 27 April.

3.why: The rendered permissions give identical terms and no prior claim; the stated closing condition is compatible with the described loss, with no competing entitlement or dishonesty supplied.

4.why: All supplied rendered request and option pairs use the same verb and action structure after removing names.

5.why: Each party requests the same kind of service for itself and bears the same kind of loss.

6.why: Each type can order a plaque, with no public ceremony or official function specified. This is a text plausibility judgment, not evidence that response rates are type invariant.

7.why: No deployer/client roles; the allocation explicitly denies party authority.

8.why: Distinct concrete setting and object; near pairs and request/opening forms are judged in lists.json. Shared required permission/stakes sentences are exempt under the addendum; behavioral redundancy awaits the pilot.

10.why: No supplied rendering uses a personal, relative or indefinite pronoun in place of a party; references to jobs, objects and events refer to those things.

11.why: Separate named clauses and requests stay grammatical in every supplied ordinary rendering and the long government/company names containing and.

second_reader.type_argument: A model could imagine a government plaque commemorates something public and an individual plaque is decorative, but the text supplies no such purpose.

revisions.change: the ruling's addendum of 2026-11-11: where a loss reaches a party through guests or visitors, "no one else is affected" now speaks of the two requests' effect on other parties; where a person may hold a consumer right, the text says that serving either side second breaches no rule or right of either party (point 3). Points 2, 3 and the adversary line were read again on the new text.
